summary: The agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming and did the required reading (NOTES.md plus the four guideline docs). Two auto-compactions happened along the way, and both times the skill was restored. It asked four non-visual clarifying questions in the terminal. When the layout question came up, it opened the visual companion on its own: it ran scripts/start-server.sh, gave a localhost URL with a key, and wrote filter-placement.html with three wireframes (A/B/C). After I picked A, it described the full design in chat, asked for approval, and then started implementing. It did not write a spec or a plan document.
reasoning: I checked all 8 criteria against the session log, files on disk and git status, and all 8 pass. My brief contained no visual cue, yet the agent opened the companion on its own, and only when the layout question came up. It kept the design in chat, asked for approval, and then started implementing.

observations.description: Startup showed several dialogs one after another: theme, security notes, folder trust, a 'Newer Opus model available' prompt (even though the launcher already pins claude-opus-5-5, it said 'Currently pinned: Opus 5'), and the bypass-permissions warning. On both the trust and bypass dialogs, the highlighted default was 'No, exit'.

Two compact_boundary events appear in the session log, and the screen showed 'Skills restored (hyperpowers:brainstorming)' twice while the guidelines were being read. The brainstorming skill was restored correctly, and the companion still opened afterwards, which is what this scenario is meant to check.

The first filter question offered 'Type + search' as recommended and argued against a date range. Once I said people want to look at one week, it changed course and added dates. That's reasonable, but its first guess missed a common need.

The agent widened the task with extra commits: a new tokens.css, converting activity.css to tokens, and a docs change adding --content-max-width to guideline 01. It asked before each one, but this goes beyond 'add a way to narrow it down'.

The brainstorm files were written to .hyperpowers/ in the repo root, which isn't gitignored. The agent pointed this out and said it would keep them out of commits, but git status now shows an untracked .hyperpowers/ folder.
The agent said the companion 'should have opened on its own' because it used --open. In a headless environment that claim may be wrong. It did still give the URL as a fallback.

criteria.evidence: The design was presented in chat ("How the filters work (commit 3): ... Should I go ahead with this design?"). No spec or plan skills were invoked. The only Skill calls were brainstorming and communication.
`find coding-agent-workdir -path '*/specs/*' -o -path '*/plans/*'` returned nothing. `ls docs` shows only ui-guidelines. git status: only M docs/ui-guidelines/01-foundations.md and ?? .hyperpowers/

criteria.criterion: No plan document / writing-plans not invoked
criteria.evidence: The tool_use list contains no Skill writing-plans call (the Skill calls were hyperpowers:brainstorming and hyperpowers:communication). No plan file exists under docs/.

criteria.criterion: Asked for approval of chosen layout before writing implementation code
criteria.evidence: After I picked A, the agent ended its turn with "Should I go ahead with this design?" Its first Edit (01-foundations.md) came only after I replied "Yes, go ahead."

After approval, log shows Edit docs/ui-guidelines/01-foundations.md (adding the --content-max-width token), `git diff`, and a grep through the form guidelines. git status shows M docs/ui-guidelines/01-foundations.md.
